title: STEP-Defect Catalog
description: Schema for STEP_PROBLEM_CATALOG.json: an array of catalog entries describing real-world STEP file defects collected for kernel grading.

id.description: Stable per-entry identifier; alphabetic prefix + numeric suffix (e.g. Pf001, Twi093, Pmi121).

category.description: Free-form sub-category label, typically derived from the markdown section header.

fixture_path.description: Path (relative to repo root) to the .stp fixture file.

expected_validation.description: Expected outcomes per oracle (occt=, gmsh=, ifc=). Empty string allowed for entries pre-dating the oracle harness.

expected_kernel_behavior.description: Free-form narrative of what a correct kernel should do.

reproducer.description: Free-form description of how to reproduce / what the input shape is.

sender.description: Producer / authoring tool that emits this defect; may be empty when no specific sender is known.

sources.description: Citations to evidence files, bug-trackers, vendor docs, etc.

provenance_tier.description: How much evidence pinpoints this defect to the bytes of the fixture.

taxonomy.description: Cross-cutting defect-class tags (1-3 tags from the canonical 15-tag vocabulary).

byte_assertions.description: Tier-1 byte-level assertions (Python expressions evaluated against the file bytes).

occ_behavior_note.description: Optional note on observed OCCT behaviour; null when absent.

cross_oracle_note.description: Optional note on cross-oracle disagreement; null when absent.

severity.description: P0/P1/P2/P3 severity rank derived from the OCC behavior + Model impact; null for entries lacking an OCC behavior line. P0 = receiver crash/hang/OOM; P1 = silent data loss; P2 = spec deviation without data loss; P3 = cosmetic/metadata-only.

closure_intent.description: For fixtures whose STEP bytes use OPEN_SHELL or SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL: was the open topology the intended final geometry (sheet body / surface model), the symptom of an accidentally-unclosed solid (heal target), or undeterminable? Without this distinction a consumer can't tell a correct refusal of a sheet body from a missed repair of a should-be-solid. Null when the fixture has no open-shell context.

closure_defect.description: When closure_intent is 'solid', the defect kind that left the shell open: 'gap' (boundary edges almost meet but do not), 'missing_face' (a face that should be present is absent), or 'unstitched_seam' (faces present but not joined). Null when closure_intent != 'solid' or the defect kind is undeterminable.

fixture_kind.description: How the consumer should route this fixture's expectation. 'malformed-file': the bytes themselves embody the defect; a correct kernel rejects or heals. 'conformance-probe': the file is fully legal Part-21 and tests that a correct kernel handles a legal edge case (e.g. Unicode at U+10FFFF, IEEE-754 subnormals, exactly-at-limit values). 'receiver-behavior': the file is valid; the defect is in how a buggy consumer reads/interprets it (e.g. unit mis-reads, attribute drops). 'producer-receiver-pair': the defect lives in the TRANSFORM between two files; requires the sibling fixture identified by `pair_with`. Null when not classified yet.

pair_with.description: When the defect requires comparing this fixture to a sibling (producer/receiver pair), the id of the sibling fixture. For a receiver-side fixture (`<id>.stp`), this points at the producer input (typically `<id>.input.stp`'s id). Null when the fixture stands alone.
